name: Syrma
description: A star 22 parsecs away, 2.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: radius 2.641 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 9.267 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.041) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: effective temperature 6201 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.025)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: distance 22.237 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 22 parsecs away, 2.6 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 9.267 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,201 K, so 2.641 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 69701: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q
